_comment_family: The file's full name (name ID 4) rather than its family (ID 1), which
is 'Neue Montreal' - the same choice the two Telegraf packs make, and
for their reason turned around. Neue Montreal ships upstream as a
family running Thin to Bold with an italic beside each, so the family
name alone names none of them: a machine handed 'Neue Montreal' would
answer with whichever cut it happens to have, and the Regular at this
size is a caption laid out against stems that are not there. The app
carries the Bold only, so the Bold is what gets declared.
That is a fact about what is in fonts/ and not about the family, in
the way league-spartan's note is: the day a second cut is dropped in
beside this one it needs its own pack declaring its own full name,
and nothing here has to change for it.
Weight 700, which is what the file's OS/2 table says and what its
subfamily (ID 2) calls it. Asking for 800 or 900 here would invite a
browser to synthesise a weight this file does not contain, and a
synthesised weight is measured as well as drawn - the caption would
be laid out against letters nobody chose.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css. This face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON at load time (see registerFace in
js/channels.js), which is the route content/README.md describes -
nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file,
and used by the installer as the name it registers this face under
The PostScript name first, then the Windows full name. Both name this
one cut, so a machine answering to either is answering with these
letterforms. The family on its own is deliberately absent for the
reason given above - it is the name every other weight of Neue
Montreal answers to as well, and the fallback route exists to produce
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
caption laid out against the wrong metrics is broken rather than
merely different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before
anything is drawn. Chosen all the same: Neue Montreal is a
neo-grotesque, closed apertures and level terminals, which is the
family Helvetica belongs to and Arial is the copy of that every
Windows machine has. Segoe UI behind it for the machine that somehow
lacks even that, humanist rather than grotesque and so the second
Impact and Arial Black are absent for garet-book's reason: they are
display cuts drawn to be set enormous, and putting one behind a text
grotesque at caption size would make the one thing that survives a
missing file the furthest possible thing from it. The weight comes
from the font shorthand rather than from the stack, so Arial named
here is Arial Bold when this face is asked for.
